lines.text: He was a Japanese soldier posted to a small island in the Philippines.
His orders were simple: never surrender.
So when the war ended, he kept fighting.
He found leaflets dropped from planes saying the war was over.
His family flew in a plane overhead, calling to him through a loudspeaker.
It was not until 1974 that his former commanding officer flew to the island,
stood in the jungle, and ordered him to stop.
Onoda walked out of the trees, still in uniform, rifle in hand.
He had been fighting alone for twenty-nine years.
